statement: The following assertions hold. (i) Γ is an additive semigroup with one-dimensional leaves, and its generated group is exactly Λ. Every finite compatible Taylor jet is realized by sections of all sufficiently large degrees in each admissible progression. (ii) K is a full-dimensional closed convex cone, contains the positive constant ray, projects onto the whole exponent orthant, and satisfies K = int K. Its bounded-degree sections are bounded. More precisely, uniformly in the chosen point and nearby grading, |γ| := ∑ i γi ≤ CC j r ((j, γ) ∈ K). (4.6) Its scaled image has the form K̃ = {(D0, x) : x ∈ RN ≥0, D0 ≥ f(x)}, (4.7) where f is finite, positively homogeneous, convex, and f(x) ≥ cC|x| (x ∈ RN ≥0) (4.8) for a constant cC > 0 independent of the nearby grading and chosen point. (iii) In the scaled coordinates the lattice density is s. If ℓ is a linear functional strictly positive on K̃ \ {0}, then #{γ′ ∈ Γ̃ : ℓ(γ′ ) < q} = s Leb{(D0, x) ∈ K̃ : ℓ(D0, x) < 1} qn + o(qn ), (4.9) with Lebesgue measure in the scaled coordinates. No saturation assumption on Γ is required. (iv) The vector c0 = (r, 1) in the original (j, γ) coordinates (4.10) belongs to Λ. Its scaled coordinates are (N, 1).
